summary: Describes a protocol for running OSI Connectionless transport service on top of UDP. It was on the standards track and is now historic.

eli5.summary: It lets a different family's messages ride inside simple Internet packets.

questions: how to run osi connectionless transport over udp
what is osi connectionless transport over udp
what udp port does osi use
subtitle: Carrying OSI connectionless transport messages inside ordinary UDP datagrams.

tldr.problem: OSI upper-layer services offer features TCP/IP lacks, but OSI lower layers were not widely available in the Internet.
tldr.mechanism: Each OSI connectionless transport message (a UD TPDU) is sent as a single UDP datagram, with UDP standing in for the OSI connectionless network service. UDP port 102 is reserved for this.
tldr.outcome: The idea was that OSI applications could run over IP and later move to OSI lower layers. The RFC is now Historic.

today: RFC 1240 was published in June 1991 as an IAB standards-track protocol, and its status is now Historic. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Run OSI Over UDP
sections.content:
The ISO and CCITT had defined upper-layer standards for session, presentation and application services, with services such as dialogue control, transfer syntax, peer authentication and directory services that TCP/IP did not offer. Following the approach of RFC 1006, this memo offers OSI services in the Internet without disrupting existing facilities, which the authors say allows a more graceful transition from IP-based to OSI-based networks.

The specific aim is to gain experience with OSI connectionless upper-layer protocols. The RFC points to request/response client-server use as the most prominent connectionless application class, where connection setup and teardown are unneeded overhead, especially on reliable LANs and ISDN.
sections.eli5: Some useful programs were written for a different network family. This lets them run on the Internet that already exists.

sections.title: The Model
sections.content:
The memo presents a standard OSI Transport Service Access Point (TSAP) interface, as in ISO 8072 and its Addendum 1, but implements the ISO T-UNIT-DATA protocol on top of UDP. OSI connectionless upper layers operate without knowing they run over UDP/IP. In essence, UDP is the connectionless network service provider.

A TS-user uses the service, a TS-peer is the process that maps connectionless transport onto UDP, and the TS-provider is everything between the two TS-users. Because there is no negotiation before data transfer, the two users need prior knowledge of each other, such as protocol version, formats and options. Everything in ISO 8072/AD1 is supported except the Quality of Service parameter, left for future study.
sections.eli5: The program on top thinks it is using its usual delivery service. Underneath, a translator hands each message to UDP.

sections.title: Mapping Primitives onto UDP
sections.content:
UDP is assumed to offer two primitives: send datagram and read datagram. They map directly: N-UNIT-DATA.REQUEST becomes send datagram and N-UNIT-DATA.INDICATION becomes read datagram. Source and destination addresses come from the IP addresses in the calling and called TS-addresses, and quality of service is ignored.

When a T-UNIT-DATA.REQUEST is issued, the TS-peer builds a UD TPDU and sends it as a single datagram. When UDP delivers a datagram, the UD TPDU is read and a T-UNIT-DATA.INDICATION is generated.

The memo reserves UDP port 102 for applications that realize this service. As with RFC 1006, other port values may be used by prior agreement, for example through the OSI Directory.
sections.eli5: Sending a message means handing it to UDP. Getting a message means reading what UDP received. Port 102 is the agreed mailbox.

sections.title: The UD TPDU Format
sections.content:
The UD TPDU sits in the UDP data field. It has four parts: LI (octet 1), the type UD (octet 2, value 01000000), a variable part and the user data.

LI is the length of the header including parameters but excluding the LI itself and user data, with a maximum of 254. The variable part carries the source TSAP (parameter code 11000001) and destination TSAP (11000010), each with a length of at most 254. No checksum parameter is needed, since the UDP checksum already does the checking.

The OSI connectionless network service allows at most 64,512 octets of user data, further limited by the smaller maximum datagram size of the two UDP peers, which should be known by prior agreement.
sections.eli5: Each message has a short label on the front saying how long the label is, what kind of message it is, and who it is from and for.

sections.title: Security and Conclusion
sections.content: The Security Considerations section says security issues are not discussed in the memo. The conclusion expects that, as OSI lower-layer service becomes widely implemented in the Internet, the underlying UDP/IP services can be simply replaced with the OSI lower layers.
sections.eli5: The memo does not talk about safety. It hoped the temporary envelope could later be swapped for the real OSI one.
